A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HTO/OVERTONE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison; v2 retains Appendices A–C and adds Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original knowledge-editing experiments, token-level analyses, component ablations, and continual-editing results, including Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and Appendix C. Results carried forward from v1 still constitute original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: Equations (2)–(3) and Algorithm 1 retain the same filtered prediction distribution, adaptive target mixing, label-check fallback, and clipped forward-KL objective. The revised DPO interpretation does not change the implemented editing procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ZsRE, Wikirecent, Wikicounterfact, WikiBio, and MQuAKE-2002 under the same editing scenarios. MQuAKE's 1-Hop/2-Hop terminology becomes Single-Hop/Multi-Hop, with matching prompts and results rather than demonstrated additional coverage. Unlearning and longer-text applications are only proposed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: FT-M, LoRA, MELO, and WISE with and without OVERTONE, alongside ROME and MEMIT. MQuAKE still compares FT-M and LoRA variants. Newly cited methods are not added to the experiments.

E3.justification: Both retain LLaMA 2-7b-Chat and LLaMA 3-8b-Instruct, editing sequence lengths 1/10/100, and the same metrics and ablation settings. Appendix B preserves training settings and MQuAKE prompting, temperature 0.1, and generation limits of 30/200 tokens.

E4.justification: The token-loss and underfitting-degree analyses, continual-editing comparisons, and four component ablations are retained unchanged. New Appendix D provides conceptual discussion without additional ablation, robustness, or case-study evidence.

E5.justification: v2's conclusion newly clarifies that performance is averaged across editing samples and identifies multiple runs per sample as future work. This adds statistical reporting context, but no run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical result rows in Tables 1–5 match, including the appendix continual-editing tables. Figures 1–3 retain the same plots and findings. The MQuAKE column relabeling adds no result entries or performance changes.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 locally revises Theorem A.16's DPO derivation: the clipped-ReLU preference model becomes a clipped exponential model, with a normalization constant Z and an explicit expected log-preference-likelihood derivation. Several probability-ratio expressions also change. The theorem's stated conclusion and the other theoretical sections remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions remain identifying HTO, mitigating it through adaptive token smoothing, establishing theoretical advantages, and improving four editors across two LLMs. Added application suggestions and future directions do not establish new central contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendix D explains extension difficulties for ROME/MEMIT and acknowledges unresolved knowledge conflicts and optimal-target selection. Section 2.3 adds a rationale for greedy decoding, while the introduction and conclusion add prospective applications and the repeated-run reliability limitation. Existing result interpretations remain intact.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same EasyEdit implementation information, editor-specific hyperparameters, OVERTONE settings, and evaluation prompts. No new hardware, runtime, code-access, or data-access information is supplied; changed hop labels do not establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds PEFT/ReFT and retrieval-augmented-generation references and an Overfitting and Mitigation paragraph comparing OVERTONE with in-context distribution targets and neighboring-knowledge perturbation work, including Qi et al. and Ma et al. These refine the retained positioning of token-level smoothing as complementary to existing editors.

P1.justification: Most prose and the section sequence are retained. v2 expands several explanations and the conclusion, adds Appendix D and a related-work paragraph, changes hop terminology, and updates authorship and conference front matter, including acknowledgments and an impact statement.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout, substantially resizing and relocating figures, tables, and Algorithm 1. Title, typography, headers, and appendix table placement also change. The existing empirical displays are retained, with revised MQuAKE column labels.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through concrete applicability and knowledge-conflict limitations in Appendix D, clearer positioning against related overfitting methods, and acknowledgment of the need for repeated-run evaluation. Appendix A.4 also develops the preference-likelihood interpretation more explicitly. These are limited explanatory gains: the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged, and run-level uncertainty is still unreported.
